citeAs: Hauret, J., Olivier, M., Joubaud, T., Langrenne, C., Poirée, S., Zimpfer, V., and Bavu, É. (2024). Vibravox: A Dataset of French Speech Captured with Body-conduction Audio Sensors. Submitted to Elsevier Speech Communication.
creator: Julien Hauret, Malo Olivier, Thomas Joubaud, Christophe Langrenne, Sarah Poirée, Véronique Zimpfer, Éric Bavu (Conservatoire national des arts et métiers / French-German Research Institute of Saint-Louis)
description: Vibravox is a GDPR-compliant dataset of French speech captured with five different body-conduction audio sensors (two in-ear microphones, two bone conduction vibration pickups, and a laryngophone) plus an airborne reference microphone. It contains 45 hours per sensor of speech samples and physiological sounds recorded by 188 participants under different acoustic conditions imposed by a high-order ambisonics 3D spatializer. The dataset includes four subsets (speech-clean, speech-noisy, speechless-clean, speechless-noisy) along with annotations about recording conditions and linguistic/phonetic transcriptions.
name: Vibravox
publisher: Laboratoire de Mécanique des Structures et des Systèmes Couplés (LMSSC), Conservatoire national des arts et métiers (Cnam)
rai:annotatorDemographics: 188 participants (97 female, 91 male). Age range: 18-82 years. Female mean age: 25.9 years, median: 22 years. Male mean age: 31.4 years, median: 27 years. Overall mean age: 28.55 years, median: 25 years. A deliberate effort was made to recruit a diverse and gender-balanced group.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Text transcriptions were sourced from the French Wikipedia subset of Common Voice and filtered to remove proper names (except common first names, French town/region/country names), numbers, Greek letters, mathematical symbols, and syntactic errors. Text normalization included lowercasing and removing punctuation except apostrophes. Phonetic transcriptions in IPA (33 French phonemes) were generated using the CoML lab text phonemizer. Words unrecognized by the phonemizer underwent manual phonetic transcription. Recording condition annotations were also included.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is limited to French language, restricting generalizability to other languages. The participant pool shows age imbalance (female mean age 25.9 vs male mean age 31.4 years). The speech-noisy subset is limited in size (approximately 1h34 training data) compared to speech-clean. The Lombard effect (speakers increasing vocal effort in noisy conditions) means reported signal-to-external-noise ratios represent a lower bound. Some participants had ear canal anatomies incompatible with the rigid in-ear microphone, leading to inadequate acoustic sealing. A deliberate effort was made to recruit a diverse and gender-balanced group of participants.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from 200 participants (188 retained after post-processing) in a controlled recording environment using a 3D sound spatializer (spherical array of 56 loudspeakers, radius 1.07 m). Participants wore six simultaneous audio sensors recorded by a Zoom F8n field recorder at 48 kHz / 32-bit. The recording protocol consisted of four steps per participant: (1) speech-clean: reading French Wikipedia sentences for 15 minutes; (2) speechless-noisy: remaining silent for 2 minutes 24 seconds in a noisy environment; (3) speechless-clean: remaining silent for 54 seconds in complete silence; (4) speech-noisy: speaking for 54 seconds with ambient noise from in-house ambisonic recordings.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Out of 200 participants, 188 were retained (6% excluded). Out of 30,568 initially collected sentences, 28,471 were retained (6.8% of sentences excluded). Issues included mispronounced sentences, sensors shifting from initial positions, occasional sensor malfunctions, and instances where a microphone was inadvertently left unequipped. In some cases, such as when a participant's ear canal was too small for the rigid in-ear microphone to achieve proper acoustic sealing, the automatic filters were not triggered.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Six simultaneous audio channels recorded at 48 kHz and 32-bit resolution using a Zoom F8n field recorder. Sensors include: headset microphone (Shure WH20XLR), forehead accelerometer (Knowles BU23173-000), in-ear soft foam microphone (Knowles FG-23329-P07), in-ear rigid earpiece microphone (Knowles SPH1642HT5H), throat microphone (iXradio XVTM822D-D35), and temple vibration pickup (AKG C411). A 20 Hz high-pass filter was uniformly applied to each acquisition channel during recording.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is exclusively in French, limiting applicability to other languages. Body-conducted sensors exhibit inherent low-pass filtering characteristics, limiting bandwidth. The speech-noisy subset lacks a clean reference signal, making it unsuitable for direct supervised training of speech enhancement models. The temple vibration pickup has very limited bandwidth (below 1500 Hz). Some participants had ear canal anatomies incompatible with the rigid in-ear microphone. The dataset was recorded in a controlled laboratory environment with a 3D spatializer, which may not fully replicate all real-world acoustic scenarios.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The speechless-noisy subset can be dynamically mixed with speech-clean recordings to simulate noisy conditions while retaining a clean reference. The dataset is split by speaker (80% train, 10% validation, 10% test) with no speaker overlap. VAD timestamps were extended by 0.6 seconds on both sides to eliminate artifacts at segment edges.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Post-processing filtering was applied to the speech-clean subset using three automatic filters: (1) Phoneme Error Rate (PER) filter: discards samples where PER > 10%, computed using Levenshtein distance between labeled and Whisper-derived phonetic transcriptions; (2) SNR filter: discards samples where SNR[i,j] = Lspeech_50[i,j] - Lsilence_50[i,j] ≤ 1.5 dB; (3) Sensitivity drift filter: discards samples where Lspeech_50[i,j] ≤ Lsilence_50[i]. VAD timestamps were extended by 0.6 seconds on both sides; in rare cases where adjusted timestamps exceeded audio boundaries, audio was trimmed by 15 ms. The dataset was split by speaker: 80% training, 10% validation, 10% test, with no speaker overlap between splits.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables research into robust communication systems for noisy environments, with applications in military operations, industrial settings, and emergency services. It supports development of voice command systems for heavy machinery safety. The biometric richness of body-conducted speech data opens applications in access control and intelligence gathering. The dataset was designed to be GDPR-compliant, with informed consent, anonymization, and encryption of participant data. A deliberate effort was made to recruit a diverse and gender-balanced group of participants to increase representativeness and inclusivity.
rai:dataUseCases: Speech enhancement / bandwidth extension for body-conducted speech; automatic speech recognition (speech-to-phonemes/text); speaker verification; heart rate tracking and vital sign monitoring (using speechless-clean subset); voice commands development; generating synthetic datasets with realistic physiological and sensor-inherent noise; comparative analysis of different body-conduction sensor technologies; robust communication systems for noisy environments (military, industrial).
rai:machineAnnotationTools: whisper-timestamped model (speech-to-text engine based on Whisper with dynamic time warping applied to cross-attention weights) was used for Voice Activity Detection and word timestamp prediction during post-processing filtering. The CoML lab text phonemizer was used to generate IPA phonetic transcriptions from text.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Voice recordings (biometric data) from 188 participants. Age and gender information collected (Table VII shows age statistics by gender: female mean age 25.9 years, male mean age 31.4 years, ages ranging 18-82). All data was processed in accordance with GDPR, including informed consent, anonymization, and encryption during storage and analysis.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: The paper does not specify a number of independent annotations per item; transcriptions are single-source (Wikipedia text + automated phonemization).
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No inter-annotator agreement metrics or annotation quality analysis is described; transcriptions are derived from source text and automated tools.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No annotation platform (e.g., MTurk, Label Studio) is mentioned; annotations were generated from Wikipedia source text and automated phonemization tools.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation of missing values is described in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning, update cadence, or maintenance plan is described beyond the initial release.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific dates or time period for data collection are mentioned in the paper.
